title: Garbled/incorrect value of q in the n=15 worked example (should be q=1897/27≈70.259)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Severity: minor / expository (factual error in worked example, not a logical gap).**

In the Cardano section, immediately after the boxed formula (eq. cardano), the worked example at $n=15$ contains a garbled and numerically wrong expression for $q$:

> "$q=-\tfrac{83}{27}\cdot 11+\dots$"

The correct value from eq. (pq), $q=\dfrac{3382-99n}{27}$, at $n=15$ is
$$q=\frac{3382-99\cdot 15}{27}=\frac{3382-1485}{27}=\frac{1897}{27}\approx 70.259.$$

All the OTHER numbers quoted in the same example are correct and consistent with $q=1897/27$: $p=-16/3$, $R=q^2/4+p^3/27\approx 1228.47$, $u_+=-q/2+\sqrt R\approx -0.0801$, $u_-=-q/2-\sqrt R\approx -70.179$, and $x=19/3+\sqrt[3]{u_+}+\sqrt[3]{u_-}\approx 1.77753$, giving $(y+x/y)x=15$ to high precision (verified: $|(y+x/y)x-n|<10^{-9}$).

So only the displayed formula for $q$ is malformed. **Fix:** replace it with $q=\tfrac{1897}{27}\approx 70.259$ (or write the symbolic form $\tfrac{3382-99\cdot15}{27}$). This does not affect any logical step but a line-by-line verifier will flag the inconsistency.
